_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning about the legal and ethical rights and responsibilities that Australian consumers and businesses have.

toLevel2.question: Australian Consumer Law gives buyers rights about refunds, repairs, and replacements when products fail to meet basic standards.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law sets out rights to refunds, repairs, and replacements when products fail to meet basic standards.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is a core feature of Australian Consumer Law at this level.

toLevel2.question: Misleading advertising is allowed in Australia and businesses can make any false claim about a product without any consequence.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Misleading advertising is prohibited under Australian Consumer Law and businesses face real consequences for false claims.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating misleading advertising as allowed misstates Australian Consumer Law at this level.

toLevel2.question: The ACCC is an Australian regulator that protects consumers from unfair business practices and enforces parts of consumer law.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The ACCC is the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, a regulator that protects consumers and enforces consumer law.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the standard description of the ACCC's role at this level.

toLevel2.question: Businesses in Australia have no legal responsibilities to their customers and can act in any way they choose at any time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Australian businesses have legal responsibilities to customers, including under Australian Consumer Law and other regulations.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating businesses as having no legal responsibilities misstates Australian law at this level.

toLevel2.question: A consumer who buys a faulty product has no link to any right to ask for a refund or repair under Australian law.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law gives buyers the right to ask for a refund, repair, or replacement of a faulty product.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating consumers as having no rights when products fail misstates Australian Consumer Law.

toLevel2.question: Ethical responsibilities of business have no link to fair trade or environmental sustainability practices in any country.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Ethical responsibilities go beyond the law and can include fair trade and environmental sustainability practices.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating ethical responsibilities as unlinked to these practices misses widely taught content.

toLevel2.question: Consumers in Australia have no right to information about a product and businesses can hide every detail at any time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law gives consumers rights to clear information and prohibits misleading conduct that hides material details.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating consumers as having no information rights misstates Australian Consumer Law at this level.

toLevel2.question: Understanding consumer rights and business responsibilities helps Australians act as more confident and protected buyers.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Understanding rights and responsibilities helps Australians act as more confident and protected consumers.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This learning outcome is widely taught at this level.

toLevel2.question: Fair trade has no link to ethical business practices and never appears in any discussion of business responsibility at any time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Fair trade is widely discussed as part of ethical business practice and supply-chain responsibility today.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating fair trade as unrelated to ethical business misses its documented role at this level.

toLevel2.question: A living wage is a wage high enough to cover basic living costs for a worker and any dependants in their household.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A living wage is a wage high enough to cover basic living costs for a worker and any dependants.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the standard description of a living wage at this level.

toLevel2.question: Environmental sustainability has no link to any ethical responsibility of any Australian business in any setting at any time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Environmental sustainability is widely discussed as a recognised ethical responsibility of Australian businesses today.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating environmental sustainability as unrelated to business ethics misses widely taught content.

toLevel2.question: Both legal and ethical responsibilities matter to Australian businesses because law sets minimum standards while ethics often exceed them.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Law sets minimum standards while ethics often exceed them, so both matter to Australian businesses.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This pairing is widely taught at this level.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes Australian Consumer Law?
toLevel2.correct: A national law that gives consumers rights to refunds, repairs, and replacements when products fail basic standards
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law gives consumers rights to refunds, repairs, and replacements when products fail basic standards.

distractors.answer: A national law that allows businesses to make any false claim about any product without any consequence at all
distractors.explanation: False claims are prohibited under Australian Consumer Law, not allowed.

distractors.answer: A national law that applies only to children under twelve and never affects any adult consumer in any setting
distractors.explanation: Australian Consumer Law applies broadly to consumer transactions, not only to children.

distractors.answer: A national law that has no link to any business in any sector and never enforces any standard at any time
distractors.explanation: Australian Consumer Law applies across many sectors and is enforced by regulators.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is the role of the ACCC in Australia?
toLevel2.correct: The ACCC enforces consumer law and protects buyers from unfair or misleading business practices across many sectors
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The ACCC enforces consumer law and protects buyers from unfair or misleading business practices.

distractors.answer: The ACCC sets the price of every product in every Australian shop in every region in every year of trading
distractors.explanation: The ACCC does not set product prices; markets and businesses do.

distractors.answer: The ACCC operates only one shop in one suburb and has no role in any other part of the Australian economy
distractors.explanation: The ACCC is a national regulator, not a single-suburb shop.

distractors.answer: The ACCC has no link to any consumer protection in Australia and never enforces any law in any year ever
distractors.explanation: The ACCC plays a central role in Australian consumer protection and enforces laws.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is a basic right under Australian Consumer Law when a product fails basic standards?
toLevel2.correct: The right to ask for a refund, repair, or replacement of the faulty product from the seller in many cases
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The right to ask for a refund, repair, or replacement of a faulty product is a core consumer right.

distractors.answer: The right to keep the product and pay an extra fee to the seller in every Australian shop each year today
distractors.explanation: Consumers do not pay extra fees as a basic right when products fail.

distractors.answer: The right to receive a free unrelated product from a different shop in a different state at no cost ever
distractors.explanation: Consumer Law does not entitle buyers to free unrelated products from other shops.

distractors.answer: The right to set the price of every other product in the same shop for the rest of the financial year
distractors.explanation: Consumers do not gain price-setting rights over other products in a shop.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is misleading advertising under Australian Consumer Law?
toLevel2.correct: An advertisement that makes a false claim about what a product can do or where it was made or how it is sold
toLevel2.correctExplanation: An advertisement that makes a false claim about a product is misleading advertising under Australian Consumer Law.

distractors.answer: An advertisement that gives accurate information about a product's price, features, and country of origin clearly
distractors.explanation: Accurate information about a product is not misleading advertising.

distractors.answer: An advertisement that uses bright colours but makes no factual claim about the product on display today
distractors.explanation: Bright colours alone with no factual claim do not constitute misleading advertising.

distractors.answer: An advertisement that simply lists the name of the product and the address of the shop selling it
distractors.explanation: Listing a product name and shop address without a false claim is not misleading.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes an ethical responsibility that goes beyond Australian law?
toLevel2.correct: A business voluntarily pays its workers a living wage that covers basic living costs for them and their families
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Voluntarily paying workers a living wage is an ethical responsibility that often goes beyond legal minimums.

distractors.answer: A business pays its workers nothing at all and refuses to provide any pay slip in any month of any year today
distractors.explanation: Paying workers nothing breaches Australian wage law; it is not an ethical responsibility.

distractors.answer: A business runs only one advertisement each year and refuses to provide any product to any customer at any time
distractors.explanation: Refusing to provide products is not an ethical responsibility; it is the absence of business activity.

distractors.answer: A business has no link to any worker in any country and never sets any pay rate at any time at any stage
distractors.explanation: Businesses with workers do set pay rates; the no-link claim is wrong.

toLevel2.question: Why is it useful for an Australian consumer to know their rights under Australian Consumer Law?
toLevel2.correct: Knowing rights helps a consumer act with confidence, ask for remedies when products fail, and avoid being misled
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Knowing rights helps a consumer act with confidence, ask for remedies, and avoid being misled.

distractors.answer: Knowing rights has no link to any consumer choice in any sector at any stage of any year in any setting at all
distractors.explanation: Consumer rights are closely linked to consumer choices.

distractors.answer: Knowing rights always guarantees that every product a consumer ever buys will be perfect in every way today
distractors.explanation: Knowing rights does not guarantee every product is perfect; it gives recourse when products fail.

distractors.answer: Knowing rights always removes every choice from every Australian consumer in every region in every year today
distractors.explanation: Knowing rights expands rather than removes choice.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes fair trade as an ethical business practice?
toLevel2.correct: Sourcing goods in ways that pay producers fairly and support better working conditions in supply chains overseas
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Fair trade sources goods in ways that pay producers fairly and support better working conditions in supply chains.

distractors.answer: Sourcing goods only from the cheapest supplier with no regard for any worker condition in any country at all
distractors.explanation: Cheapest-only sourcing without regard to worker conditions is the opposite of fair trade.

distractors.answer: Sourcing goods at random with no link to producer pay or worker condition in any country at any stage of trade
distractors.explanation: Random sourcing without consideration of conditions is the opposite of fair trade.

distractors.answer: Sourcing goods only from one suburb in Australia and refusing to import any good from anywhere overseas at all
distractors.explanation: Fair trade is broader than refusing imports; it focuses on conditions in supply chains.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is a legal responsibility that Australian businesses have to consumers?
toLevel2.correct: Not engaging in misleading or deceptive conduct in advertising or sales under Australian Consumer Law
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Not engaging in misleading or deceptive conduct is a core legal responsibility under Australian Consumer Law.

distractors.answer: Promising every customer a free unrelated product worth at least one thousand dollars at every transaction
distractors.explanation: Businesses are not required to give customers free thousand-dollar products at every transaction.

distractors.answer: Refusing to provide any information about any product to any customer at any time during any sale
distractors.explanation: Businesses must provide accurate information; refusing all information would breach consumer law.

distractors.answer: Paying every customer a salary every fortnight regardless of whether the customer ever buys any product
distractors.explanation: Businesses do not pay customers salaries; customers pay businesses for products.

toLevel2.question: Which scenario best illustrates a consumer exercising their rights under Australian Consumer Law?
toLevel2.correct: A buyer returns a kettle that broke on first use and asks the seller for a refund or repair under the law
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Returning a faulty kettle and asking for a refund or repair is a clear example of exercising consumer rights.

distractors.answer: A buyer keeps a kettle that broke on first use and pays the seller an extra fee for a replacement on the spot
distractors.explanation: Paying extra for a replacement is not exercising consumer rights under the law.

distractors.answer: A buyer refuses to ever shop again at any Australian retailer in any region for the rest of their life
distractors.explanation: Refusing to shop is not exercising consumer rights for the faulty product.

distractors.answer: A buyer stands outside the shop for two days and refuses to enter the shop in any year at any stage
distractors.explanation: Standing outside a shop is not exercising consumer rights under the law.

toLevel2.question: Which list includes only ethical responsibilities of business that often go beyond Australian law?
toLevel2.correct: Fair trade sourcing, environmental sustainability, paying a living wage, and supporting fair conditions in supply chains
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Fair trade, sustainability, living wage, and supply-chain fair conditions are widely discussed ethical responsibilities.

distractors.answer: Setting prices by random draw, ignoring every supplier, and refusing to provide any product to any customer at all
distractors.explanation: These actions are not standard ethical responsibilities of business.

distractors.answer: Refusing to follow any law, ignoring every consumer, and never producing any goods or services in any sector at all
distractors.explanation: Refusing to follow laws is the opposite of ethical responsibility.

distractors.answer: Painting office walls in bright colours, holding free public concerts, and operating without any worker in any year ever
distractors.explanation: Office colours and free concerts have no link to ethical business responsibilities.

toLevel2.question: Why does the ACCC investigate businesses suspected of misleading consumers?
toLevel2.correct: To enforce Australian Consumer Law, protect buyers from harm, and hold businesses accountable for their conduct
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The ACCC investigates to enforce Australian Consumer Law, protect buyers, and hold businesses accountable.

distractors.answer: To set the price of every product in every Australian shop in every region in every financial year today
distractors.explanation: The ACCC does not set product prices; markets and businesses do.

distractors.answer: To run a single shop in one suburb without any link to any other business in any year at any stage of trading
distractors.explanation: The ACCC is a national regulator, not a single-suburb shop.

distractors.answer: To pay every Australian consumer a salary regardless of whether the consumer ever buys any product or service
distractors.explanation: The ACCC does not pay consumers; it enforces consumer protection law.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes the link between legal and ethical responsibilities of Australian businesses?
toLevel2.correct: Law sets minimum standards while ethics often go beyond the law to include fair trade and sustainability commitments
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Law sets minimum standards while ethics often go beyond the law into fair trade and sustainability.

distractors.answer: Law and ethics are identical in every detail and businesses always face the same standards from both sources today
distractors.explanation: Law and ethics differ; ethics often go beyond legal minimums.

distractors.answer: Law applies only to one suburb in Australia and ethics never apply to any business in any country at any time at all
distractors.explanation: Law applies broadly across Australia and ethics apply to many businesses.

distractors.answer: Law and ethics have no link to one another and businesses can ignore both without any consequence in any year ever
distractors.explanation: Law and ethics are linked, and businesses face consequences for breaching either.

toLevel3.question: A consumer dispute about a faulty product is resolved only when the consumer pays the business an extra fee in any year of operation.

toLevel3.question: Ethical business practices have no link to fair supplier pay, responsible sourcing, or worker support in any supply chain.

distractors.answer: True

toLevel3.question: Mia buys a kettle that breaks on first use. Which idea best fits her rights under Australian Consumer Law?
toLevel3.correct: She can ask the seller for a refund, repair, or replacement because the kettle has failed basic consumer guarantees
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Asking for a refund, repair, or replacement is a core right under Australian Consumer Law for faulty products.

distractors.answer: She must keep the kettle and pay an extra fee to the seller because consumers have no rights when products fail
distractors.explanation: Australian Consumer Law gives clear rights when products fail; consumers do not pay extra fees as a remedy.

distractors.answer: She can ignore the seller and pay another shop to fix the kettle without any link to consumer law in any year

distractors.answer: She must wait one year before contacting the seller and then accept any outcome the seller offers without question

toLevel3.question: Jarrah sees an advertisement claiming a product treats a serious illness when there is no evidence for the claim. Which idea best fits this case?
toLevel3.correct: The advertisement is likely misleading conduct under Australian Consumer Law and the ACCC may investigate the claim
toLevel3.correctExplanation: False medical claims are likely misleading conduct under Australian Consumer Law, and the ACCC may investigate.

distractors.answer: The advertisement is fully legal because every Australian business can make any false claim about any product today

distractors.answer: The advertisement is unrelated to consumer law because Australian law applies only to refunds for broken products
distractors.explanation: Australian Consumer Law covers misleading conduct, not only refunds for broken products.

distractors.answer: The advertisement always guarantees that every Australian consumer will buy the product without any further question
distractors.explanation: Advertising does not guarantee purchases; consumers still choose.

toLevel3.question: Anika reads about an Australian business that pays its workers a living wage even though the law allows lower pay. Which idea best fits this practice?
toLevel3.correct: The business is meeting an ethical responsibility that goes beyond the legal minimum wage under Australian law today
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Paying a living wage above the legal minimum is an ethical responsibility that goes beyond the law.

distractors.answer: The business is breaking Australian law because every business must pay below the legal minimum wage every year today

distractors.answer: The business has no link to any ethical responsibility because law and ethics are identical in every detail every year

distractors.answer: The business is ignoring every worker because paying a living wage is the same as paying nothing at all in any country
distractors.explanation: Paying a living wage is paying workers more, not paying them nothing.

toLevel3.question: Sam reads about a business that sources coffee through a fair trade scheme. Which idea best fits this practice?
toLevel3.correct: The business is taking ethical responsibility for working conditions and pay in the coffee supply chain overseas
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Fair trade sourcing is ethical responsibility for working conditions and pay in the coffee supply chain.

distractors.answer: The business is breaking Australian law by sourcing coffee under any fair trade scheme in any country today
distractors.explanation: Fair trade sourcing is not against Australian law.

distractors.answer: The business has no link to any working condition because fair trade is the same as ignoring every worker today
distractors.explanation: Fair trade focuses on worker conditions, not ignoring them.

distractors.answer: The business is operating without any supplier because fair trade always means the business has zero suppliers
distractors.explanation: Fair trade businesses do have suppliers; fair trade is about how those suppliers are treated.

toLevel3.question: Lila is told that 'Australian businesses have no legal responsibility to customers'. Which response best fits the topic?
toLevel3.correct: The claim is misleading because Australian Consumer Law sets out clear legal responsibilities to customers in many cases
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law sets out clear legal responsibilities to customers; the claim is misleading.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every Australian business in every region operates with zero responsibility to any customer
distractors.explanation: Most Australian businesses have legal responsibilities to customers.

distractors.explanation: Australian Consumer Law applies broadly, not to a single suburb.

toLevel3.question: Kofi reads that the ACCC has taken legal action against a business for misleading conduct. Which idea best fits this action?

toLevel3.correctExplanation: The ACCC enforces Australian Consumer Law to protect buyers from unfair or misleading practices.

distractors.answer: The ACCC is operating one shop in one suburb without any link to any consumer in any region at any stage
distractors.explanation: The ACCC is a national regulator, not a single-suburb shop.

distractors.answer: The ACCC has no link to any consumer protection and never takes any legal action in any year in any setting
distractors.explanation: The ACCC takes legal action when needed; the no-link claim is wrong.

toLevel3.question: Yen wants to compare a legal responsibility and an ethical responsibility of an Australian business. Which idea best fits the comparison?

toLevel3.correctExplanation: Law sets minimum standards while ethics may go beyond the law into fair trade or sustainability.

toLevel3.question: Rosa is told that 'consumers in Australia have no right to information about any product'. Which response best fits the topic?

toLevel3.correctExplanation: Australian Consumer Law gives consumers rights to clear information and prohibits misleading conduct.

distractors.explanation: Australian consumers have had information rights for many years under consumer law.

toLevel3.question: Amir reads about an Australian business that runs an environmental sustainability program. Which idea best fits the program?

distractors.explanation: Environmental sustainability is widely discussed as an ethical responsibility.

toLevel3.question: Jade is asked to evaluate a claim that 'a living wage and a legal minimum wage are exactly the same amount'. Which response best fits the topic?

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because legal minimum wages are always set above every living wage in every state in every year today
distractors.explanation: Legal minimum wages may sit below or near living-wage estimates, not always above them.

toLevel3.question: Linh wants to compare misleading advertising and accurate advertising in Australia. Which idea best fits the comparison?

toLevel3.correctExplanation: Misleading advertising makes false or deceptive claims that can breach consumer law; accurate advertising states truthful information.

distractors.explanation: Misleading advertising is prohibited under Australian Consumer Law.

toLevel3.correctExplanation: Publishing warnings about scams and unsafe products is part of the ACCC's work to inform consumers and prevent harm.
